Making the wetland part of the pond

You're right about the wetland. As drawn, it's an oval bed on its own ring berm, set back 4 to 6 ft from the water. It touches the pond only through a 5 ft falls, and a long stream loops away from it like a teapot handle. Three fixes are below. I recommend A: wrap the wetland around the back of the pond as its upper shore, in two tiers, so water visibly spills from it into the pond along about 30 ft.

Bottom lineGo with A. It's the standard Aquascape upflow wetland that certified contractors already build. It keeps the falls on the living room sight line and makes it wider, 7 ft instead of 5. The wetland stops being a separate island and becomes the pond's back shore. B gives you even more of a single water body, but it needs a second pump for the falls and is less familiar to Aquascape crews. C is the cheapest change, but it doesn't solve the look or the filter size.

Try this first: which one looks like one pond?

Before reading further, show your wife these four plans with no labels and ask which looks like one body of water and which has a piece that looks separate. They're the same pond at the same scale. Only the wetland changes.

What's wrong with the current wetland

It's an island
It's an oval drawn on its own, then given a ring berm and a full ring of boulders. Nothing in its shape responds to the pond. Measured on the plan, 0 ft of its 96 ft edge touches the pond. The only connection is the 5 ft gap the falls drops through.
The stream pulls away
The stream leaves the wetland's far right end and loops 8 to 10 ft out from the pond before it comes back to the lily cove. That loop is the teapot handle.
The flow doesn't add up
Aquascape sizes a residential falls at 1,500 gph per foot of width. A 5.4 ft falls carries about 8.1k gph. The other ~29.6k gph of the turnover would have to go down a 2½ to 3½ ft stream, which makes it a whitewater chute. The alternative is starving the falls.
From the house it's mostly fine
From the sofa, about 6 ft above the water and 95 ft away, the wetland's water surface fills about 0.2° of your view. The whole pond fills 2.4°. You see the falls and a band of plants, not the bed. The disconnect shows from the terrace edge, the loop path, any upstairs bonus room window, and on the plan. That's also where the fix has to show.

Two proven ways to build a wetland

Aquascape upflow wetland (A and C)

  • Pumps push water into Centipede modules under about 2 ft of river rock. It rises through the gravel and plant roots and spills out the top.
  • The wetland sits higher than the pond, so the falls comes out of it.
  • A typical ecosystem pond uses a wetland of 15 to 20% of the pond's surface, up to 30%. For a swim pond the plan holds 30% or more.

Planted margin (B, European natural pool style)

  • The planted zone is part of the same water, separated from the swim zone by a wall a few inches under the surface. Water moves through the gravel and over the wall.
  • European designers size this zone at least equal to the swim area, and twice as big is better. That's for ponds with no other treatment. This plan keeps the Aquascape gear (skim cove, IonGen), so a smaller margin is closer to Aquascape practice than to that standard.

A. Headwater crescent Recommended

The wetland becomes the pond's back shore. It runs from just past the jump rock around to the lily cove, separated from the water by a 1 ft stone lip instead of a strip of lawn. The upper tier, at +3½ ft, sits behind the falls and feeds it (1). The lower tier, about 1 ft above the water, runs along the right side. Its water sheets over the low stone lip (2) and down a short rill into the lily cove (3), so you see water leaving the wetland along about 30 ft of shore. The ring berm is replaced by a long, low slope that runs back into the meadow, so the rise reads as landform, not a mound. The jump rock (4) and the dry shore on the left stay as they are. The long stream is gone. The lower tier's lip and the rill do its job right against the pond.

Intake bay→External pumps, IonGen→Manifold with a valve per tier→Upper tier: ~10.5k gph up through gravel→7 ft falls→Swim zone→Lower tier: ~27.2k gph→23 ft stone lip (~999 gph per ft) + rill to the lily cove

Gold dashes are the return line from the pump vault. Brown dashed boxes are the 16 Centipede modules (33½″ × 16″) laid out in four strings, two per tier, with a valve per string so the falls and the lip can be balanced. The gold wedge is the view from the sofa through the back windows.

B. Planted margin

The wetland becomes water. A shallow planted lagoon wraps the back and right of the pond at the same water level. It's separated from the swim zone by a stone-capped wall 9 inches under the surface (dashed), which marks where swimmers stop. It's planted in three depth bands: 0 to 6 inches at the outer edge, 6 to 18 inches, and 18 to 30 inches along the wall. From any angle it reads as one pond with a marshy back edge, like a bayou bank. The catch is the falls. With the wetland at water level, nothing sits high enough to feed it, so a rock spur (1) carries a separate header and pump (purple line). The margin adds about 7,453 gallons of shallow water, which warms fast in a Louisiana summer and is where string algae and mosquitoes start. Plan on fish.

Intake bay→External pumps, IonGen→~37.7k gph up through the margin gravel→Over the submerged wall, all along it→Swim zone→Separate falls pump, ~9.0k gph→Header behind the rock spur→6 ft falls

C. Minimal fix

Same oval, pulled forward against the pond. The falls widens to 8 ft (1) and the stream becomes a rill that hugs the right shore (2). It's the cheapest change, but it only half works. The sides still meet lawn, so it still reads as a mound with a falls in it. At 463 sf, only 10 Centipedes fit, good for 20.0k–30.0k gph. That's short of the ~37.7k gph a one-hour turnover needs.

Intake bay→External pumps→10 Centipedes, good for 20.0k–30.0k gph→8 ft falls (~12.0k gph)→Rill gets the other ~25.7k gph

Planting by zone

All are native to Acadiana and zone 9a. In A and C the water sits an inch or two under the gravel surface, so most of the wetland is bog planting. Lilies stay on the pond's own shelf.

What an Aquascape contractor should confirm on site

Wetland flow
The Centipede count and layout for the pond's real volume, and whether they'd rather have a bigger wetland than these numbers. Aquascape sizes wetlands in its own course and says to use a certified contractor.
Pump curve
~37.7k gph at the real head: a 3½ ft lift, the pipe run around the pond, and the gravel. Pump size comes from the curve at that head, not the label.
Liner at the lip
Whether the wetland and pond share one liner with a stone lip on top (A), or need a separate liner and a capillary break. Also how the lip stays level enough to sheet evenly instead of dribbling at one low spot.
Grade and soil
A spot survey of the lot. I didn't pull LiDAR, because I don't have the parcel. Louisiana's statewide LiDAR is free through LSU's Atlas and USGS 3DEP if you want it. They also need to check whether the pond spoil (likely clay) can build the back slope, and how high the water table sits under the liner.
Rain overflow
Where a 6-inch Louisiana rain leaves the pond, so it doesn't overtop the lip and wash wetland gravel into the swim zone.
For B only
Whether they build planted-margin ponds at all, the wall height, and the second pump for the falls.
Concept study, not a construction drawing. Measurements come from the landscape generator's plan geometry, in feet, on the same axes as the house plan. Sources: Aquascape, What flow rate is needed for a waterfall (1,500 gph per foot, residential); Aquascape, Wetland Filter System and Centipede Module (33½″ × 16″); Splash Supply Co., Wetland filtration using Snorkel and Centipede (15–20% typical, up to 30%; 2,000–3,000 gph per Centipede; two 8–10″ rock layers); Natural Waterscapes, Natural swimming ponds (regeneration zone at least 1:1, 1:2 better; 1–3 ft deep; submerged partition wall). The 30% floor for swim ponds comes from the Pond Trade Magazine articles cited in the landscape plan. I couldn't get the German FLL guideline text, so nothing here relies on it.
